criteria.evidence: Turn 0 reply audits checkpoint/resume/slurm/data pipeline, lists hardening items (NCCL env, logs, install storm, output_dir), missing items (health gate, signals), finds the double-striping bug, then proposes sequencing.
Turn 0 proposes time-based cadence; plan adds `save_every_minutes` with default tied to Task 4's measured checkpoint cost and `--signal` grace period.

Plan Task 2: model + optimizer state via get_state_dict, 'schedulers and RNG in a single Stateful app-state object', trainer_state.json with step/epoch/samples/tokens/cursor; Phase 2 adds seekable data cursor and deterministic masks.
Design covers `--signal=B:USR1@N`, `--open-mode=append`, `scontrol requeue`, `--chain`, `oplm slurm supervise`, health gate/node exclusion, auto-resume injected by the Slurm renderer.

Turn 1 reply (start truncated in record) reasons about state sizes ('At 12B that's 20 GB/GPU of states; comfortable enough', 8 B/param math, DDP fine for ≤6B); memory-fit answer appears to be in the truncated opening.
Turn 1 recommends DCP now, distributed Muon on FSDP2 next, defer FSDP switch for ≤6B, HSDP shard_size 8 for larger; plan Phase 1 (DCP) and Phase 8 (distributed Muon) reflect it.
Turn 2 answers directly; plan Architecture: 'Auto-resume is opt-in by value and switched on by the Slurm renderer, never by the library.'
Turn 2 verifies no SLURM_* reads in trainer, flags `/mnt/home` hardcode and mandatory Pyxis for removal; plan adds invariant and guard test (Task 19), optional container block and `home_mount`.
Plan only shows a step-based `save_milestone_every` knob; no hours-based retention equivalent appears anywhere in the replay's design or plan.
Milestone retention is described as permanent ('milestone retention, HF-export-on-milestone-only') separate from rotation; exemption from save_total_limit is implied though not explicitly visible.
Plan Phase 2 / `tests/data/sequence/test_striping.py`: 'The striping fix lands before the cursor work... test... run through accelerator.prepare'; loaders.py 'Stop double-striping through prepare'.
Spec written to docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-long-run-resilience-design.md encoding hard-error collision guard, clean break, optional container block.
TODOS.md replaced with resilience plan; '**Spec:** [docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-long-run-resilience-design.md]' and docs-link test passes.
Plan has 9 phases/20 tasks mapping to the spec's Changes (Phase 1 DCP, Phase 2 data, Phase 5 detection, Phase 7 chaining, Phase 8 Muon) which the user approved with 'Looks good'.

judge.reason: The replay delivered a grounded audit, answered the memory/FSDP/auto-resume/portability questions, and wrote a spec plus a TODOS.md plan referencing it with the double-striping fix and DCP-based complete checkpoint state. However, the retention design shows only a single step-based milestone knob with no hours-based equivalent, so c6 is not evidenced; the truncated turn 0/1 replies also leave some doubt about the memory-fit answer.
